findings.reason: the clause is the section's only server-visible check that a relation exists, so as written a node can pass while the delivered endpoint (two signals related by what they are to each other) is absent, and the fix is to assert the relation itself (a distinct relation kind or a tool that reports it) rather than mere co-membership.
findings.text: the clause "Through a running server, a walk from one setpoint signal chosen beforehand, which the private file names, returns the signal it is measured against" cannot fail: the server's context tool (`fetch_signal_context` in imas_codex/tools/plant_search.py:255-315 as it stands today) pages siblings by `CANDIDATE_PLANT_COMPONENT` membership — `s.id <> $resource AND EXISTS { MATCH (s)-[:CANDIDATE_PLANT_COMPONENT]->(:PlantComponent {id: $component_id}) }` — so it already returns every signal on the same component, including the one measured against, before any relation is written; the section could deliver no relation of this kind and still pass that clause

findings.reason: adding the count of excluded signals, and requiring it to equal the decided/conflict/undecided totals the role vocabulary already computes for the same population, is what makes the exclusion checkable instead of asserted.
findings.text: the Delivers promises that "a signal whose role is undecided or in conflict is related to nothing and is counted", but the done-when's partition covers only signals whose role was decided (received at least one relation, or none), so a run that relates an undecided or conflicted signal is neither counted nor caught

response_events.reason: The node's dispatch contract carries it: the walk must return the measured-against signal as a typed relation with its kind and rule, and the same walk before the run, or with the relation removed, must not return that typed relation.
